title: The universal form
hookLine: Arjuna asks to see Krishna's true form and is overwhelmed

lines: LET ME SEE YOU AS YOU ARE.
cards: Two armies are lined up, ready to fight. Between them sits a chariot with two people in it. One is Arjuna, a warrior who has lost his nerve.
The other is his charioteer, Krishna, who has spent a long conversation teaching him. By now Arjuna has heard enough to suspect that his driver is far more than a driver.
So he asks: if it's possible, let me see you as you really are. It's a request people make of friends, of lovers, of God. This time, it's granted.

teach.h: A DIVINE EYE TO SEE WITH.
teach.b: This is chapter eleven of the Bhagavad Gita, a Hindu scripture, and it unfolds in four movements. First, the eyes.

Krishna tells Arjuna that he can't see this with his ordinary eyes, so he gives him a divine eye, a new way of seeing. Awe here isn't something you squint at; you need different eyes for it. Second, the sight.

teach.h: THE WHOLE UNIVERSE IN ONE FORM.
teach.b: Arjuna sees the whole universe gathered in one body: countless faces and eyes, ornaments and weapons, the gods themselves, all of it in one form.
A narrator reaches for the brightness: if the light of a thousand suns rose in the sky at once, he says, that might come near the splendor of it. Third, the shaking.
Arjuna's hair stands on end. He bows his head and folds his hands. As the vision goes on, it turns terrifying: worlds and warriors rushing into blazing mouths like rivers into the sea.
Arjuna admits he's lost his bearings and can find no peace. Fourth, the way back. Near the end Arjuna says he's glad to have seen what he had never seen before, and yet his mind is shaken with fear.

teach.h: SHOW ME THE FAMILIAR FORM AGAIN.
teach.b: He asks to see the familiar form again, the one he knows.
Krishna gently returns to it, and Arjuna says he is himself again. That's the honesty of this chapter. The vision is real, and it's too much.
Hindu readers hear many things here, but the story never pretends that seeing everything is comfortable.

how: Hindus read and recite the Bhagavad Gita, and the vision of chapter eleven is painted and sculpted as Krishna's universal form, often shown with many heads and arms.

o: a sage who wrote down the Bhagavad Gita
the charioteer who drove Krishna into battle
the warrior who asked to see Krishna as he is

games.q: you're Arjuna. you've seen the whole universe in one body, and it's more than you can bear. what do you ask?
o: to see even more of it.
to see the familiar form again.
to forget you ever saw it.
games.why: Arjuna asks to see the familiar form again, and Krishna gently returns to it.

practice: Find the biggest thing you can see from where you are, a long street, a crowd, every leaf on one full tree, and try to take in all of it at once; notice that you can't, and let that be fine.
When it gets to be too much, come back to something small and familiar, your hand or the floor, the way Arjuna asked for the form he knew, and then look out again.

wordCard.voice: Arjuna. The warrior who asked to see Krishna as he really is, and was left overwhelmed by the whole universe in one body. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the all-form, the universal form, the name given to the vision in Bhagavad Gita 11.
